The handlers Django installs keep the file they are building as their `file` attribute, set in `new_file`, and the parser answers both exceptions by closing the `file` of every handler that has one (`django/http/multipartparser.py:MultiPartParser._close_files`).

`MemoryFileUploadHandler` decides once, in `handle_raw_input`, whether it will keep the files: it sets its `activated` flag to whether the body is no larger than `settings.FILE_UPLOAD_MAX_MEMORY_SIZE`, 2,621,440 bytes by default (`django/core/files/uploadhandler.py:MemoryFileUploadHandler.handle_raw_input`).

Not activated, it hands each chunk on unchanged and returns no file, and `TemporaryFileUploadHandler` writes the chunks to a temporary file and returns a `TemporaryUploadedFile` (`django/core/files/uploadhandler.py:MemoryFileUploadHandler`).

The note of 29 bytes went to disk with the scan because it arrived in a large request: a file is kept in memory only when the whole body is small enough (`django/core/files/uploadhandler.py:MemoryFileUploadHandler.handle_raw_input`).
